title: Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement - uibc-core verifier

check_id_absent_from_report.S9: declared in the specification as head pinned out-of-band, listed in docs/EVIDENCE-INDEX.md as not covered (no test constructs it), and never emitted in a verify report: the report jumps S8 -> S11
check_id_absent_from_report.S10: declared in the specification as ttestation closure declared, listed in docs/EVIDENCE-INDEX.md as not covered, and never emitted in a verify report

http.fields: full after patch 0001; before patch: subject/trust_level/spec_version/limitations/not_checked dropped
http.anchoring: unavailable: endpoint accepts no key or DID, so every HTTP verdict is trust_level=unanchored

hmac_sha256_v02.reason: symmetric: verification requires the owner key

explicitly_not_capable: returning PASS for a package it cannot evaluate (the JS implementation never returns PASS; this one does)
anchoring over the HTTP transport (no key/DID parameter)
attesting key custody (key_custody is null in the observed report)
lifecycle event signature verification (listed in not_checked)
behavioral evaluation and memory fidelity (listed in not_checked)
claiming the third-party corpus as our own: the vectors, the manifest and the reference verifier belong to its author
non_claims: a PASS is not a statement that the package is valid; it is a statement that no violation was detected within the observed evidence boundary
the report does not sign anything and does not assert third-party approval
the presence of 10 checks is not a claim that 10 is the complete set (see check_id_absent_from_report)

third_party_corpus_runs.corpus_owner: third party, not the operator of this implementation; reference verifier ships with the corpus
third_party_corpus_runs.contract: <cmd> <vector-file>; exit 0 = valid; last stdout line one JSON object {verdict, codes, result, tiers}

comparison_surface.note: A vector's conformance column is its verdict, its result token where the manifest declares one, both tier columns where it declares them, and the behaviour assertions. Its reasonParity column is the code comparison, which vectors/MANIFEST.json calls a datum rather than a failure. The status column still counts both, so the exit code has not moved.

third_party_corpus_runs.measured: verdict and result are normative; failure codes are the corpus's own vocabulary, so a code difference is a reason-parity datum, not a failure
